concepts.name: Editorial arrival
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create realistic production-quality CourtWork desktop UI at 1440 x 1024. Current date September 9, 2026; synthetic data only. Art direction: Clean and Cool, noticeably more expressive and freely composed than the attached CURRENT implementation, which is grounding for product facts, not a pixel target. Sophisticated cool-white, graphite, pale silver surfaces; disciplined elegant typography, generous but useful whitespace. No decorative dashboards, gradients, colorful status pills, stock photos, cards inside cards, or oversized generic SaaS headline. Use only spacing, alignment and typography first; borders for inputs/selected/floating/error, very restrained elevation. 14-16px readable body text, max two fonts. One focused primary screen, one main task, no invented capabilities. Flat full-bleed app content, no browser chrome or mock laptop. Preserve product name CourtWork; real brand glyph in reference only, never invent a new logo. Chat and Work are user terms; internal Session/Matter/Runtime/adapter words stay out of normal UI. Exact statuses remain text, colors never claim acceptance. Configuration saved, connection tested, execution completed, and accepted work are different facts. Do not include visible concept names or numbering. Do not blindly reproduce incidental typography or exact blank areas of reference. Finish all content cleanly within canvas.
Concept name: Editorial arrival. Redesign the populated Home from attached screenshot with much greater compositional freedom. Maintain a recognizable slim 256px sidebar and brand, only New chat, Home, find field, Northside Housing and Coastal Freight projects, bottom Settings. In main surface a small understated date and greeting near the upper quarter, composed asymmetrically but on a coherent reading grid. Headline 28px 'What would you like to work on?' and a wide elegant input 'Describe the work you want to do…' with Local test and send control. Below it one concise line Project Northside Housing and Ask before editing. Composer is the primary anchor but lift its center to about 38% viewport height so an actual waiting item is visible without scrolling. Below, a quiet 'Waiting for you' row: 'Retainer letter — Okafor', 'Northside Housing', 'Answer requested', open chevron. Then 'Continue' list of just two other existing chats: 'Rent ledger reconciliation' with text 'Failed'; 'Exhibit index rebuild' with 'Completed'. Completed items belong in Continue not 'In progress'. No duplicate same chat rows, no invented aggregate counts/date analytics or calendar. All rows use the same stable existing chat identity, a visual grouping proposal only. Clean cool editorial rhythm, refined inset input, strong list readability, relaxed yet efficient composition. This is a proposed change to current Home geometry, not a current screen.

Concept name: Connection atelier. Redesign Settings Models as a beautiful light, precise configuration studio, grounded in attached Models screen but dramatically reduce documentation clutter and nested panels. Keep sidebar and a restrained Settings rail with General, Appearance, Models selected, Tools & Integrations, Skills, Memory, Permissions, Keyboard, Developer. In main content 'Models'. One current connection row 'Local test' / 'Current default' / 'No key needed', quiet Configure. A spacious distinct area 'Preview an endpoint', Base URL field 'http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1', optional API key field blank with text 'Optional'. Primary action 'Fetch models', quiet 'Test connection' secondary. These actions are backend-supported BE-17/18 but frontend integration is proposed, so add nearby concise sentence 'Preview only. This endpoint will not be saved.' No save endpoint action on this temporary preview. Below one subtle helper: 'Testing checks endpoint reachability, not model execution.' No green success state or fetched model results because this is the form BEFORE request. Keep a separate collapsed 'Advanced' disclosure. Current default applies to new chats only, shown once. Developer details live behind a quiet 'Connection details' link or disclosure; no internal API enum values or giant In force card. NO list of multiple saved connections, no rename, no display name field, no connect/enable custom endpoint: BE21 not implemented. No numbered roadmap steps. Striking crisp alignment, very thin silver field borders, precise dark buttons. Current saved local test and unsaved preview visibly separate using hierarchy not giant containers.

Concept name: Evidence reading room. Redesign the current NDA Review shown in attached screenshots into an elegant full-width work reading mode. Replace modal-on-dimmed-chat appearance with a continuous paper surface in the main region; existing left app sidebar remains. This is a new visual proposal requiring shell review, not a screenshot of shipped functionality. The main hero is the recorded source excerpt, with a compact complementary review column, not a chat transcript. At top 'NDA review' and 'Return to chat'. Below 'Confidentiality term' large restrained editorial typography. Scope line 'Candidate pending · Source revision 1'. Source text: '4. Term. These confidentiality obligations continue for three years after the Effective Date.' Set beautiful 16px readable document text, max65 characters per line. Quiet source label 'Recorded source · revision 1' with separate 'Source details' disclosure for full identity and offsets. Use the EXISTING source text excerpt, never invent PDF page number or filename or rendered page geometry. Adjacent narrow review column: '1 unresolved rule', selected 'Term duration — Unknown'; smaller '3 other rules — Pass' as a collapsible summary. Exact explanation 'The term duration is explicitly unknown.' Below a subtle note 'Recorded facts still need confirmation.' The quote says three years but recorded facts are unknown, so do not reconcile that by appearance or claim verified. A clearly labelled Reason textarea with helper 'Recorded with your decision.' Primary 'Request evidence', quiet secondary 'Reject'. NO Accept button at all: this unresolved candidate does not advertise accept. Propose a revision as quiet disclosure. No green approved/ready badge, no completeness percentage or model vote, no auto acceptance. Distinct precise graphite-white editorial layout, left aligned content with quiet silver rule, one unobtrusive candidate identity disclosure. Preserve candidate/source versions and decision authority. This is a focused review layout, not a generic dashboard or a new product.
